prompt: Choose the correct option.
context: Please be quiet. Mia ___ an online lesson right now.
explanation: Right now describes an action in progress, so use the present continuous.
theory: Present continuous: am/is/are + verb-ing for an action happening around now.
hint: Look at right now.

prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct verb form.
explanation: Use have + past participle with I. Never goes between the auxiliary and the participle.
theory: Present perfect: have/has + past participle. Use it for life experience when no finished time is given.
hint: There is no finished past time.

prompt: Correct the sentence.
context: We have visited the museum last Saturday.
answer: We visited the museum last Saturday.
explanation: Last Saturday is a finished past time, so the past simple is required.
theory: Use the past simple with a stated, finished past time such as yesterday or last Saturday.
hint: Focus on the time phrase.

prompt: Rewrite in the passive voice.
context: People speak English in many countries.
answer: English is spoken in many countries.
explanation: The object English becomes the subject; present simple passive is is + past participle.
theory: Passive voice: be in the correct tense + past participle. Include the agent only when it matters.
hint: Start with English.

prompt: Complete with the correct form of SUCCESSFUL.
explanation: Completed is a verb, so it is modified by the adverb successfully.
theory: Adverbs commonly modify verbs. Many are formed with adjective + -ly.
hint: Ask what kind of word modifies completed.

prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
answer: If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train
explanation: The third conditional describes an unreal past situation and its imagined result.
theory: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.
hint: Build the if-clause first.

prompt: Select every sentence that can express a strong present deduction.
options: She must be at work.||She can't be at work.||She might be at work.||She should be at work.
answer: She must be at work.||She can't be at work.
explanation: Must expresses strong positive deduction; can't expresses strong negative deduction. Might is only a possibility.
theory: For present deduction: must + base verb for strong certainty; can't + base verb for strong impossibility.
hint: Choose both positive and negative strong deductions.

prompt: Match each relative word with its usual reference.
explanation: Who refers to people, which to things, where to places, and whose shows possession.
theory: Relative clauses add information about a noun. The relative word is chosen by meaning and grammatical role.
hint: One item shows ownership.

prompt: Choose the correct article.
context: I saw ___ unusual bird near the lake.
explanation: The noun is singular and first mentioned; unusual begins with a vowel sound.
theory: Use a/an for one non-specific singular countable noun. Choose an before a vowel sound.
hint: Listen to the first sound of unusual.

prompt: Report the sentence.
answer: Lena said that she was feeling tired.||Lena said she was feeling tired.
explanation: In past reporting, am feeling normally backshifts to was feeling and I changes to she.
theory: Reported speech often backshifts the tense when the reporting verb is in the past.
hint: Change both the pronoun and the tense.

prompt: Complete with the comparative form of RELIABLE.
context: This train service is ___ than the old one.
explanation: Reliable is a longer adjective, so form the comparative with more.
theory: Use -er with many short adjectives; use more with most longer adjectives.
hint: Do not add -er to reliable.

prompt: Choose the best form.
context: By next June, I ___ this course.
options: will finish||will have finished||am finishing||have finished
explanation: By next June sets a future deadline before which the action will be complete.
theory: Future perfect: will have + past participle for an action completed before a future point.
hint: Look at by + future time.

prompt: Choose the closest meaning of allocate.
context: The manager allocated extra time to the new project.
options: ignore||set aside for a purpose||measure carefully||use immediately
explanation: To allocate something is to officially set it aside for a particular purpose.
theory: allocate /ˈæləkeɪt/ (verb): to give time, money, or resources for a particular purpose.
hint: Think about distributing a limited resource.

prompt: Complete with the target word.
context: The school will ___ more money to language classes next year.
explanation: Allocate fits because money is being assigned to a specific purpose.
theory: allocate (verb): assign a resource to a person or purpose.
hint: It begins with allo-.

prompt: Choose the best definition of reliable.
context: A reliable colleague always keeps promises.
options: expensive||easy to replace||able to be trusted||usually late
explanation: Reliable describes a person or thing you can trust to work or behave well.
theory: reliable (adjective): consistently good and able to be trusted.
hint: Think about someone who keeps promises.

prompt: Complete with the target word.
context: Planting trees can help ___ the effects of urban heat.
explanation: Mitigate means make something harmful less severe.
theory: mitigate (verb): to reduce the seriousness or harmful effect of something.
hint: The meaning is close to lessen.

prompt: Choose the closest meaning of carry out.
explanation: Carry out means perform or complete a task, plan, or experiment.
theory: carry out (phrasal verb): perform or complete something planned.
hint: Scientists do this to experiments.

prompt: Complete with the correct form of COMPEL.
context: She gave a ___ argument for changing the policy.
explanation: Compelling is the adjective meaning very convincing or holding attention.
theory: compelling (adjective): convincing, powerful, or difficult to ignore.
hint: The blank describes argument.

prompt: Match the word with its meaning.
options: journey=>the act of travelling from one place to another||trip=>a visit that includes going somewhere and returning||destination=>the place someone is going to||route=>the way used to get from one place to another
explanation: These words describe different parts or types of travel.
theory: Journey focuses on movement; trip on the whole visit; destination on the end point; route on the path.
hint: Separate the path from the end point.

prompt: Arrange the words to make a natural sentence.
answer: We managed to meet the deadline on time
explanation: Meet a deadline is the natural collocation meaning finish by the required time.
theory: meet a deadline: finish work no later than the required date or time.
hint: The sentence starts with We.

prompt: Select all words closest in meaning to scarce.
explanation: Scarce means not available in sufficient quantity. Plentiful and abundant are opposites.
theory: scarce (adjective): insufficient for demand; hard to find or obtain.
hint: Choose two words meaning not enough.

prompt: Replace the underlined idea with a natural phrasal verb.
context: They postponed the meeting until Friday.
answer: They put off the meeting until Friday.
explanation: Put off means postpone. In the past simple, put does not change form.
theory: put off (phrasal verb): delay doing something or move it to a later time.
hint: The past form is the same as the base form.

prompt: Choose the closest meaning of ubiquitous.
context: Smartphones are now ubiquitous in large cities.
options: very expensive||found everywhere||difficult to operate||recently invented
explanation: Ubiquitous means present, appearing, or found everywhere.
theory: ubiquitous (adjective): seeming to be everywhere.
hint: Think of something you see in almost every place.

prompt: Complete with the target word.
context: The proposal received ___ support from local businesses.
explanation: Substantial support means a large or important amount of support.
theory: substantial (adjective): large in amount, value, or importance.
hint: It begins with sub-.
